<!-- ## Pre-class prep -->

<!-- No pre-class prep before our first day of class! -->

Today we run a complete data science workflow together, from a data file on the course
website to a finished chart, before anybody in the room knows how the individual pieces
work. Playing the whole game means going through the entire thing once, roughly, so that
the next eight days have somewhere to attach.

Class runs 10:00 to 4:30, and the morning comes in two parts. First we meet Positron, the
application we write every line of code in for the next nine days. Positron runs in a
browser on a Bren server, so bring your UCSB login and install nothing tonight. Then we
cover just enough Python to read the afternoon's code: what a variable is, what a string
is, and how to print one so it tells you something.

In the afternoon we play the game on daily Arctic weather from Toolik Lake in Alaska,
running from June 1988 to December 2018. By 4:30 you will have imported that file, explored
it, grouped it, aggregated it, drawn a chart from it and exported the result. We do not
clean it, because nothing in this file needs cleaning and Day 4 is the day we spend on
cleaning. Some of the afternoon will feel like copying. It is copying, and on the first day
copying is the right way to work.

## End-of-day practice

Tonight you run the same workflow again on your own, changing a few things to see what
happens. Nobody expects you to understand every line yet. Today we teach one skill, which
is reading working code and changing it on purpose, and you will use that skill every day
for the rest of the course.

- [{{< fa pencil title="A pencil" >}} **Day 1 Practice:** Rerun the Whole Game](eod-practice/eod-day1-2026.qmd)
